prompts.liquid: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one high-fidelity desktop screenshot mockup, landscape 16:10, for BOX3D Engineering Studio. A polished physically credible interactive 3D engineering laboratory, photographed-quality 3D render, fully buildable procedural apparatus. Brand: warm ivory UI, graphite text, subtle thin borders, restrained vivid orange controls, tiny technical monospace captions. No purple, no holograms. Composition: 60px full-width ivory top bar with BOX3D left, a centered study picker labeled "LIQUID DYNAMICS", small "Reference" and "Export" actions right. Narrow 60px left icon rail. Main viewport takes roughly left 72 percent with an elevated three-quarter 38 degree perspective of the entire apparatus. Right 290px tall ivory inspector panel titled "LIQUID DYNAMICS" with tabs "Set up", "Material", "Test", some clear parameter controls and a prominent orange "Run experiment" button at bottom. Bottom slim ivory playback strip with play, reset, time, scrubber and 1x selector. Small unobtrusive response cards at lower left of viewport. The scene is an elegant sunlit industrial test hall: tall steel-framed windows behind, worn pale concrete floor, soft warm daylight from upper left, grounded contact shadows, metallic edge highlights, actual material textures, modest depth of field, no blur on the apparatus. SCENE: A long shallow open-topped transparent flow tank on a dark graphite steel laboratory bench. The tank runs left to right, 6 metres long by 2 metres wide, turquoise water visibly deeper behind a vertical stainless sluice gate at the left third. Gate half raised, coherent shallow wave rolling toward two round steel obstacle posts in the downstream right half. Foam only at the wave crest and obstacles, no giant splash. Clear glass sidewalls have a steel corner frame. Adjustable feet, bolted tank base, orange hand wheel on gate screw, a pump unit and hoses at the far side. See the moving water surface and tank floor clearly. Show water physically contained by the glass tank. Show clear physical load paths, plausible wall thickness, no disconnected rails, no floating parts, no machinery fused through the specimen. The machine dominates the viewport and is entirely in frame. Understated engineering product design, calm legible interface, realistic physical materials. All labels should be short, correctly spelled, and part of the flat application interface. No other panels or competing scenes, no multi-image collage, no watermark.
